context.why: This is the foundational phase of the assessment upload workflow. The data assessment team will upload one completed GHFDB template at a time through the portal's own pages, and every story that follows depends on the record, the states, the roles and the reporting layer you build here. Nothing user-facing is in your scope. The reader that parses a template already exists and works; you are giving it a checking mode and giving the workflow its data model.
context.environment: Python 3.13 via Poetry. The worktree's virtualenv is already synced (global-heat-flow-database-K3xPiQpH-py3.13). Prefix every command with `poetry run`. Run tests with `poetry run pytest`. The lint gate is `poetry run pre-commit run -a`, never raw ruff: raw `ruff check .` is red at main by design. Full suite takes about 105 seconds.
spec_sections: spec.md Key Entities (Assessment, Data Assessor, Data Curator, Submitted file, Assessment state)
prior_decisions: D5: the check cannot be turned off. There is no setting, parameter or URL that writes without checking first.
D6: confirmation re-checks rather than trusting a stored report. The assessment's state is the idempotency key.
D7: every submitted file is kept, including rejected ones. Files are rows against the assessment, not a field on it.
D11: groups come from a data migration, never a fixture, and nothing is pinned by permission primary key.

D12: THE LOAD-BEARING ONE. The checking mode runs both import passes for real and rolls the outer transaction back. NEVER pass dry_run=True to either resource. specs/004-import-upload-template/decisions.md D16 tested this: import_data() wraps each resource in its own savepoint and dry_run=True rolls it back before the next pass runs, so the child pass cannot see the parent rows it resolves against, and every file is refused including clean ones.
D13: superseded views are deleted in the same phase that changes the record. The tree must never hold two answers at once.

acceptance.given_when_then: Given the repository, When the test suite runs, Then tests/test_review/ exists mirroring project/review/ with __init__.py at each level and a conftest.py, per constitution Article VI.

Given the new test tree, When a test needs an assessment, a claimed person, a ghost person or a publication, Then a factory-boy factory supplies it, reusing the framework's own factories where they exist rather than redefining them.

Given project/review/states.py, When any transition is attempted, Then every legal transition from data-model.md succeeds and at least one illegal transition per state is refused, including a non-curator attempting to reach COMPLETE from AWAITING_DECISION.
Given project/review/permissions.py, When is_data_assessor or is_data_curator is called, Then it answers correctly for a user in each group, a user in neither, and a user in both.

Given a fresh database, When migrations run, Then the Data Assessor and Data Curator groups exist, the migration is idempotent on a second run, no auth.permission row is pinned by primary key, and project/review/fixtures/ghfdb_review_group.json and its commented loaddata hook in config/settings.py are gone.

Given the Review model, When migrations run, Then uploaded_by, state, decided_by, decided_at and decision_comment exist with verbose_name and help_text through gettext_lazy, the old status values are migrated into state, and status no longer exists.
Given an assessment with several submissions, When its current submission is read, Then it is the most recent SubmittedFile row, and every earlier submission remains retrievable.

Given a clean multi-site template file and check_only=True, When import_ghfdb_template runs, Then it reports what would have been written, reports no failures, and the database holds nothing afterwards. Neither pass is called with dry_run=True.

Given a GHFDBImportOutcome, When it is turned into a report, Then the counts separate sites from determinations and created from updated, and each failure carries its row number and the template's own column heading from project/ghfdb/columns.py.

Given a file carrying a value outside a known controlled vocabulary, When it is checked, Then the reported reason names the supplied value and the vocabulary it failed against. A bare 'invalid value' fails this test.

Given the tree after T005 and T006, When `poetry run python manage.py check` runs and the suite runs, Then both pass and no reference to STATUS_CHOICES, review__status or a Reviewers group survives anywhere in project/, asserted by a test rather than by eye.

verified_base.note: Full suite green in about 105 seconds, pre-commit clean, mypy clean, deptry clean. The lint step reports failed on a run where pre-commit reformats files and passes on the next run; that is the hook rewriting, not a defect. If the tree is red on arrival, STOP and report it rather than fixing it: the base was verified at this exact commit.

rituals: Read specs/005-assessment-upload-workflow/spec.md, plan.md, data-model.md and tasks.md before writing anything.
Read project/review/ in full — models.py, views.py, forms.py, admin.py, urls.py, menus.py and templates/ — before changing any of it.
Confirm HEAD equals the verified_base commit before starting.
Work in thin slices: each slice leaves the suite green and is committed before the next begins.
prohibitions: Never pass dry_run=True to either import resource. This is the one mistake this brief exists to prevent.
Never weaken or delete a test you did not author in this story.
Do not build any view, form, template or URL for the user-facing pages. That is US-1 to US-6 and not your scope.
Do not rename the framework's 'Data Administrators' group or touch Person.is_data_admin.
Do not add a notification framework or any new dependency.
Do not push, open pull requests or comment on GitHub. Commit locally only.
Do not edit files under specs/ other than appending to your own notes if asked.
